jasper: Hey team -- quick sanity check. I'm updating the GPU nodepool TF to support mixed spot + reserved capacity. Plan is: reserved capacity for baseline (p4dn x2) and spot for scale (g5/g4). Questions: 1) do we use an AWS Capacity Reservation + Launch Template, or just reserve on-demand instances and let ASG fill the rest with spot? 2) Any gotchas wiring the instance role to read the KMS key for secrets?

maria: I'd prefer using a small capacity reservation for critical baseline nodes. Capacity reservations are explicit and guarantee the capacity in the AZ. Spot is fine for burst. :thumbsup:

alex: For EKS I usually create a Launch Template with `capacity_reservation_specification` + `instance_market_options` for spot on the ASG. TF snippet looks like:```resource \"aws_launch_template\" \"gpu_lt\" {  image_id = \"ami-...\"  instance_type = var.instance_type  capacity_reservation_specification {    capacity_reservation_preference = \"open\"  }  instance_market_options {    market_type = \"spot\"    spot_options {      max_price = \\\"\\\"    }  }}``` Then mixed policy in the nodegroup/ASG.

leila: Note: capacity_reservation_preference = \"open\" makes it use any matching reservation. If you create a targeted reservation (specific instance type), match the LT. Also watch AZ placement: reservation is AZ-scoped.

jasper: Good point on AZ. We want baseline in 2 AZs. So we'd create 2 targeted reservations (one per AZ) for p4dn. Would that require separate LTs per AZ?

maria: You can use one LT but reservations are still AZ-scoped. ASG has to target subnets in the AZ with the reservation. In TF we usually create `aws_ec2_capacity_reservation` resources and set `availability_zone` accordingly. Example:```resource \"aws_ec2_capacity_reservation\" \"baseline_p4_az1\" {  instance_type = \"p4d.24xlarge\"  availability_zone = \"us-west-2a\"  instance_count = 1  instance_platform = \"Linux/UNIX\"}``` Then LT's `placement` can reference AZ? The ASG will prefer those subnets.

alex: On the secrets wiring: ensure the instance profile (node role) has `kms:Decrypt` and `ssm:GetParameter` (if using SSM). We usually attach an inline policy to the node instance role. Don't put KMS keys in user-data, read from SSM at boot.

leila: Also add a K8s bootstrap secret mount if you need to provide a service token to the node bootstrap script. But prefer IAM role + IRSA for pods. For node-level secrets, make the node role minimal.

jasper: Which is the recommended path if we want some nodes to be immutable for certain workloads (e.g., pinned models)? Reserve p4 for pinned, and label those nodes `gpu=reserved` and add taints?

maria: Exactly. Reserve p4 instances, label `gpu-class=baseline` and taint `gpu=reserved:NoSchedule`. Then node selector on the DaemonSet/Pods. That gives predictable latency for critical models.

alex: One more gotcha: Spot interruptions. For GPUs it's brutal — use `node-termination-handler` and warm pool of on-demand baseline nodes as Maria suggested. Also set `capacityRebalance` on ASG if using spot to proactively rebalance.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: New terraform plan created by jasper in branch `infra/nodepool-gpu-resv` — https://ci.example.ci/plan/12345 :rocket:

jasper: thanks. I'll update the TF with `aws_ec2_capacity_reservation` per AZ + single LT for spot config + ASG mixed policy. I'll add the node labels/taints in the bootstrap script and attach minimal KMS/SSM permissions to the instance profile. pinging for quick review @maria @alex :eyes:

maria: happy to review PR, will look today.

alex: I'll sanity-check the LT/ASG pieces. If you link the PR here I can give inline comments.

jasper: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/987 — thanks all

leila: quick note: verify the billing alert for reserved capacity changes so finance isn't surprised.

jasper: good call, will add a cost tag and notify finance.

maria: :thumbsup:

alex: :shipit:
